title: Spaghetti bolognese
description: Slow-cooked meat sauce with carrot, onion and a splash of red wine. Make a double batch and freeze half.

steps.text: Chop the onion, carrot and celeriac very finely, and chop the garlic.
steps.tip: The finer the vegetables, the more they melt into the sauce.

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot on medium heat and soften the vegetables for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.

steps.text: Turn the heat up, add the meat and garlic and cook for about 8 minutes, breaking up the meat with a spoon, until browned.
steps.tip: Let it sit for a minute at a time so it browns rather than steams.

steps: Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add the passata, oregano, salt and {150 ml} water.

steps.text: Simmer gently with the lid half on for 45 minutes, stirring now and then.
steps.tip: Longer is better: the sauce gets richer. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.

steps.text: Near the end, cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente. Keep a mug of the pasta water, drain and toss the spaghetti with the sauce.
steps.tip: A splash of pasta water helps the sauce cling. The sauce keeps 4 days and freezes well.

steps: Serve with grated parmesan.

title: Lasagne
description: Layers of pasta, rich meat sauce, creamy white sauce and melted mozzarella, baked until bubbling.
steps: Chop the onion, carrot and garlic finely. Heat the olive oil in a large pan on medium heat and soften the onion and carrot for 8 minutes.
Turn the heat up, add the meat and garlic and brown for about 8 minutes, breaking it up. Add the passata and {1 tsp} of the salt and simmer for 30 minutes.

steps.text: Make the white sauce: melt the butter in a pot on medium heat, add the flour and stir for 1 minute.
steps.tip: This paste is a roux. It should bubble but not brown.

steps.text: Take the pot off the heat and whisk in the milk a little at a time. Put it back on the heat and simmer, whisking, for 5 minutes until thick. Season with the nutmeg and the rest of the salt.
steps.tip: Adding the milk slowly while whisking keeps it smooth. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Spread a little meat sauce in a baking dish, then a layer of pasta sheets, then meat sauce and white sauce. Repeat three times, finishing with white sauce.

steps.text: Tear the mozzarella over the top and sprinkle with grated parmesan. Bake for 40 minutes until golden and bubbling.
steps.tip: If the top browns too fast, cover it with foil.

steps.text: Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting, so the layers hold.
steps.tip: Lasagne keeps 4 days and freezes well in portions.

title: Minestrone with beans and pasta
description: Thick Italian vegetable soup with white beans and small pasta, finished with parmesan and olive oil.
steps: Chop the onion, carrots and celeriac into small cubes and chop the garlic. Dice the potatoes and zucchini and shred the cabbage.

steps.text: Heat {2 tbsp} of the olive oil in a large pot on medium heat. Add the onion, carrot and celeriac and cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
steps.tip: This slow start gives the soup its depth. Do not let it brown much.

steps: Add the garlic and stir for a few seconds. Add the potatoes, zucchini, cabbage, tomatoes, the crumbled stock cube and {1500 ml} water. Bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes.

steps.text: Drain and rinse the beans. Add them with the pasta and cook for 10 minutes more, until the pasta is soft.
steps.tip: If the soup gets too thick, add a splash of water. Taste for salt now: the stock cube is already salty.

steps.text: Serve in bowls with grated parmesan and a drizzle of the rest of the olive oil.
steps.tip: The pasta keeps soaking up liquid, so leftovers get thicker. Add water when you reheat it.

title: Mushroom risotto
description: Creamy risotto with mushrooms and a few dried porcini for deep flavour. Parmesan and butter to finish.
steps: Soak the porcini in {200 ml} hot water for 10 minutes. Lift them out, squeeze them and chop them. Keep the soaking water.

steps.text: Crumble the stock cube into {1000 ml} hot water, pour in the soaking water (leave the last spoonful with any grit behind) and keep it warm on low heat.
steps.tip: Hot stock keeps the rice cooking evenly.

steps: Slice the mushrooms. Chop the onion, garlic and parsley.

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan on high and fry the mushrooms for 6 minutes until golden. Add the porcini and garlic for a few seconds, then lift half the mushrooms out onto a plate.
steps.tip: Do not crowd the pan, or they stew instead of browning.

steps: Turn the heat to medium, add the onion and soften it for 4 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains look a little see-through at the edges.
Pour in the wine and stir until it has almost all bubbled away.

steps.text: Add a ladle of hot stock and stir until it is almost absorbed, then add the next. Keep going for 18 minutes, stirring often.
steps.tip: Taste a grain: soft with a tiny bite in the middle. You may not need all the stock.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the mushrooms you set aside, the butter and the grated parmesan, cover and leave for 2 minutes. Scatter with parsley and serve.
steps.tip: Risotto should flow slowly on the plate. Add a splash of stock if it is too stiff.

title: Pesto pasta with green beans and potato
description: The Ligurian way: pasta, potato and green beans cooked together and tossed with basil pesto.
steps: Bring a large pot of water with the salt to the boil. Peel the potatoes and cut them into small cubes, about 1 cm. Trim the ends off the green beans and cut them in half.

steps.text: Add the potato cubes and the pasta to the boiling water together and stir. Cook for 5 minutes.
steps.tip: This suits pasta that cooks in 10 to 12 minutes. For quicker pasta, give the potatoes a few minutes on their own first.

steps.text: Add the green beans and cook until the pasta is al dente, usually 5 to 7 minutes more. The potato should be soft.
steps.tip: Squash a potato cube against the side of the pot with a spoon. If it breaks easily, it is ready.

steps: Scoop out a mug of the cooking water, then drain everything and put it back into the warm pot, off the heat.

steps.text: Add the pesto and a splash of the cooking water and stir well. The potato breaks up a little and makes the sauce creamy.
steps.tip: Do not heat the pesto on the stove: the basil turns dark and loses its fresh taste. The heat of the pasta is enough.

steps: Serve with the grated parmesan on top.

title: Chicken cacciatore
description: Hunter-style chicken braised with tomatoes, peppers, olives and rosemary. Serve with polenta or bread.
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with half the salt. Slice the onion and peppers, chop the garlic.

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pan with a lid on medium-high. Brown the chicken skin side down for 8 minutes without moving it, then turn and brown the other side for 3 minutes. Set it aside.
steps.tip: Golden, crisp skin gives the sauce its flavour. Leave it alone so it does not stick.

steps: Pour off some of the fat, leaving about a spoonful. Soften the onion and peppers in the pan for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and rosemary for a few seconds.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 1 minute, scraping up the brown bits. Add the tomatoes, olives and the rest of the salt.

steps.text: Put the chicken back, skin side up, cover and simmer on low for 35 minutes.
steps.tip: It is done when the meat pulls away from the bone easily.

steps.text: Near the end, cook the polenta in salted water as the packet says. Serve with the chicken and plenty of sauce.
steps.tip: Cacciatore keeps 3 days and tastes even better reheated.

title: Baked salmon with roasted vegetables
description: Salmon fillets roasted on a tray of potatoes, zucchini and tomatoes with lemon and herbs.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C. Cut the potatoes into small wedges.
Toss the potatoes on a large baking tray with {2 tbsp} of the olive oil and half the salt and roast for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile cut the zucchini and tomatoes into chunks. Add them to the tray with the herbs and the rest of the oil, toss and roast 10 minutes more.
Season the salmon with the rest of the salt. Push the vegetables aside, lay the salmon in the middle and put lemon slices on top.

steps.text: Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily but is still a little glossy in the middle.
steps.tip: Thicker pieces need the longer time. Press the top: it should separate into flakes.

steps: Serve straight from the tray, with the juice of any leftover lemon squeezed over.

title: Spinach and ricotta pasta bake
description: Pasta tossed with tomato sauce, spinach and ricotta, baked under mozzarella until golden.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and chop the garlic. Thaw frozen spinach and squeeze out the water.

steps.text: Cook the pasta 2 minutes less than the packet says, then drain.
steps.tip: It finishes cooking in the oven. Fully cooked pasta turns soft and mushy in a bake.

steps: Meanwhile warm the garlic in the olive oil in a large pan for 1 minute, add the passata and salt and simmer for 10 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts or warms through.
Mix the pasta with the sauce and nutmeg in a baking dish. Dot spoonfuls of ricotta all over and push them in a little.
Tear the mozzarella over the top and sprinkle with the parmesan.

steps.text: Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden in spots.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days. Add a splash of water before reheating.

title: Meatballs in tomato sauce
description: Soft beef meatballs with parmesan and parsley, simmered in tomato sauce and served with spaghetti.
steps: Chop the parsley and garlic finely. Grate the parmesan.

steps.text: In a bowl mix the meat, breadcrumbs, egg, half the parmesan, the parsley, half the garlic and {1 tsp} of the salt with your hands until even. Roll into small balls, about the size of a walnut.
steps.tip: Wet hands stop the mix sticking. Do not squeeze hard: gently rolled meatballs stay tender.

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pan with a lid on medium-high. Brown the meatballs for about 6 minutes, turning them carefully, until golden all over.
steps.tip: They do not need to be cooked through yet. They finish cooking in the sauce.

steps: Add the rest of the garlic for a few seconds, then the passata, basil, the rest of the salt and {100 ml} water. Cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes.

steps.text: Meanwhile cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente and drain.
steps.tip: Shake the pan instead of stirring so the meatballs stay whole.

steps.text: Serve the spaghetti with the meatballs and sauce, and the rest of the parmesan on top.
steps.tip: They keep 3 days and freeze well in their sauce.

title: Baked hake with potatoes and olives
description: White fish baked on thin potato slices with tomatoes, olives, capers and garlic.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Peel the potatoes and slice them thinly, about 3 mm.
Toss them in a baking dish with {2 tbsp} of the olive oil and the salt, spread them out evenly and bake for 20 minutes until they start to soften.

steps.text: Meanwhile slice the tomatoes and garlic, halve the olives and chop the parsley.
steps.tip: Using frozen hake? Thaw it in the fridge overnight and pat it dry.

steps: Lay the fish on the potatoes and cover it with the tomatoes, olives, capers and garlic. Drizzle with the rest of the oil.

steps.text: Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the fish is white all the way through and flakes easily.
steps.tip: Check the thickest piece with a fork. If the potatoes are still firm, give it a few more minutes.

steps: Scatter with the parsley and serve from the dish.

title: Chicken souvlaki bowls
description: Lemon and oregano chicken skewers with rice, cucumber, tomato, feta and garlicky yogurt.

ingredients.note: red onion if you have it

steps.text: Cut the chicken into cubes of about 3 cm. In a bowl mix the juice of half the lemon, {2 tbsp} of the olive oil, the oregano, half the garlic (grated) and the salt. Add the chicken, mix well and leave for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: You can do this in the morning and keep it in the fridge. Not longer than a day, though: the lemon makes chicken mushy.

steps.text: Meanwhile rinse the rice and put it in a pot with {450 ml} water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy. Do not peek while it cooks.

steps.text: Mix the yogurt with the rest of the garlic and a pinch of salt. Dice the cucumber and tomatoes, slice the onion thinly and crumble the feta.
steps.tip: Red onion is milder. With a regular onion, soak the slices in cold water for a few minutes to take away the sharpness.

steps.text: Heat the rest of the oil in a large frying pan or grill pan on medium-high. Add the chicken in one layer and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until golden on all sides.
steps.tip: Cut the biggest piece open: it is done when it is white all the way through. Fry in two batches if the pan is crowded, or it steams instead of browning.

steps: Fill bowls with rice, then the chicken, cucumber, tomato, onion and feta. Top with the garlic yogurt and squeeze over the other lemon half.

title: Greek baked beans (gigantes style)
description: White beans baked in a thick tomato sauce with dill, onion and plenty of olive oil. Great hot or cold.
steps: The night before, cover the beans with plenty of cold water and leave them to soak overnight.

steps.text: Drain the beans, put them in a pot with fresh water and simmer for 45 minutes until almost soft. Drain, keeping a mug of the cooking water.
steps.tip: They should be just soft but not falling apart. They finish cooking in the oven.

steps: Meanwhile heat the oven to 180 °C. Chop the onions, grate the carrot and chop the garlic.

Heat the olive oil in a pan on medium heat and fry the onions and carrot for 10 minutes until soft and sweet. Add the garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, dill, oregano, sugar and salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Mix the beans with the sauce in a baking dish. Add enough of the bean water (or plain water) to just cover them.

steps.text: Bake uncovered for 50 to 60 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the top is a little caramelised at the edges.
steps.tip: Stir once halfway. If it looks dry before the beans are creamy, add a splash of water.

steps.text: Let it rest for 10 minutes and serve warm with bread.
steps.tip: In Greece this is eaten warm rather than hot, often with feta on the side. It tastes even better the next day.

title: Lentil bolognese
description: A meat-free bolognese with brown lentils, mushrooms and tomato. Rich, cheap and good for the freezer.

steps.text: Chop the onion, carrots and mushrooms very finely and chop the garlic. Rinse the lentils.
steps.tip: The smaller the pieces, the more it feels like a meat sauce. A food processor makes this quick.

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot on medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook, stirring, for about 5 minutes until their juice has cooked away and they start to brown.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute. Add the lentils, passata, oregano, salt and {600 ml} water.

steps.text: Simmer with the lid half on for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
steps.tip: Use brown or green lentils. Red lentils fall apart and make it mushy.

steps.text: Near the end, cook the pasta in salted water as the packet says. Drain and serve with the sauce on top.
steps.tip: The sauce keeps 4 days in the fridge, so it is worth making the whole pot.
